title: Emu3: Next-Token Prediction for Image and Video Generation

questions.question: What training objective does Emu3 use across text, image, and video tokens?
options: One next-token-prediction objective over a unified multimodal vocabulary.
A contrastive image-text loss with no autoregressive decoder.
A separate diffusion schedule for images and a classifier for video.
A language-model loss for text and a frozen generator for images.
questions.explanation: Emu3 trains one autoregressive decoder with next-token loss over a shared vocabulary containing text, image, and video tokens. Separate diffusion schedules or contrastive-only objectives would not be the unified single-loss approach described.

questions.question: An image is 512x512 and the visual tokenizer reduces each spatial dimension by 8. How many image tokens are produced?
options: 32,768 tokens, from 64*512 with only one axis reduced.
64 tokens, counting only one side of the 64x64 grid.
512 tokens, from one token per image row.
questions.explanation: Reducing both 512-pixel dimensions by 8 gives a 64×64 grid, so 64×64=4,096 tokens. The 32,768 option reduces only one axis; 64 and 512 count a side or rows, not grid area.

questions.question: A 4-second clip at 8 FPS uses a 4x4 spatial reduction and a 4x temporal reduction. What video-token count follows for 256x256 frames?
options: 8,192 tokens: 32*32 spatial tokens across 8 reduced frames.
4,096 tokens: one 64*64 spatial frame only.
32,768 tokens: 64*64 spatial tokens across 8 reduced frames.
131,072 tokens: 64*64 spatial tokens across all 32 frames.
questions.explanation: The clip has 4×8=32 frames, then temporal reduction leaves 32/4=8. Each 256×256 frame becomes (256/4)^2=64²=4,096 spatial tokens, so 8×4,096=32,768; without temporal reduction the count would be 131,072. Temporal sampling reduces the frame count fourfold.

questions.question: For unconditional logit 1, conditional logit 5, and CFG weight gamma=3, what mixed logit does Emu3's formula produce?
options: 5, because gamma=3 selects the conditional logit.
1, because guidance removes the conditional signal.
questions.explanation: CFG mixes logits as uncond+γ(cond−uncond). Here 1+3(5−1)=13: the difference is 4 and scaling by 3 adds 12 to the unconditional logit. The 8 option scales the unconditional value itself instead.

questions.question: An image-generation service needs very low latency and can accept a separate image-only model. Which tradeoff does the lesson highlight?
options: Emu3 avoids token-by-token decoding by using a diffusion schedule.
Diffusion cannot produce high-quality images at 512x512 resolution.
Emu3 always generates faster because it predicts all image tokens in parallel.
Diffusion can generate images in seconds, while Emu3 autoregressive decoding may take minutes.
questions.explanation: At 30 tokens per second, 4,096 autoregressive image tokens take about 4,096/30≈137 seconds, roughly two minutes. The lesson contrasts this with SDXL’s seconds-scale image generation, trading latency for a unified model.

questions.question: Emu3 publishes separate post-trained Gen and Chat checkpoints. What do their image-generation and image-understanding pipelines share?
options: One identical weight set selected solely by changing the prompt template.
A requirement to emit image tokens and text tokens jointly at every step.
The next-token prediction framework over discretely tokenized modalities.
A diffusion-denoising objective shared across all published task checkpoints.
questions.explanation: Emu3-Gen and Emu3-Chat are separately post-trained checkpoints, so different prompts alone do not make their weights identical. They share the autoregressive next-token prediction framework over tokenized modalities, while generation predicts visual tokens and understanding produces text from visual context.
